A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Forge4D and contain readable methods, equations, experimental results, figures and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite the changed formatting and supplementary organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, interpolation, motion-prediction and metric-scale experiments, together with component ablations and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds in-the-wild evaluations, comparative timing measurements and quantitative flicker results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated static metric-gauge calculation to divide the sum by n instead of n-1, a limited revision to a training quantity. The three-stage architecture, state-token streaming, motion prediction and Gaussian fusion remain otherwise unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the formula correction changed the implementation.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on casually captured SelfCap yoga and corgi sequences and the complete VVC validation/test sets, covering nine human-object interaction scenarios. This substantially extends environmental coverage beyond the retained DNA-Rendering, Genebody and MetaHuman4D evaluations. Relabeling the existing DNA-Rendering training data as human-object interactions does not establish a training-data change.

E2.justification: V2 introduces the template-based LHM comparator in Table 3 and Figure 6. Appendix Table 11 adds cross-method speed comparisons against GPS-Gaussian, Queen, LHM+Multi-HMR, AnySplat, D-3DGS, SpaceTimeGS and L4GM, whereas v1's timing analysis profiles Forge4D alone. The comparator sets in the retained main benchmark Tables 1-2 are unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds an in-the-wild protocol using four cameras with angles ranging from 20 to 70 degrees, a TL-STD flicker metric, and an H20 comparative timing protocol with a monocular-input exception for LHM+Multi-HMR. Section 4.3 also changes the described no-fusion control from concatenation to averaging. These supplement the retained benchmark protocols and H200 timing experiment.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing component ablations with visual failure examples in Figure 7 and quantitative flicker measurements using TL-STD. It revises the Gaussian-fusion control from concatenation to averaging. The appendix analyses of camera count, sampling rate and video duration retain their settings and results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's Temporal Luminance Standard Deviation measures brightness fluctuation as an evaluation metric, rather than uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: The retained main benchmark, motion, metric-scale and sensitivity results match. V2 adds in-the-wild Forge4D PSNR values of 26.2735 for novel views and 25.4726 for novel times, H20 timing of 0.5035 seconds and 39.72 FPS with 20 interpolations, and TL-STD values of 0.9446 without fusion versus 0.5379 with fusion. The no-fusion PSNR changes from 29.0307 to 27.3459 under the revised control, not as a same-setting decline.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the mathematical definition of the static metric-gauge average from division by n-1 to division by n. The remaining mathematical framework and appendix motion annotations are retained, with no new theorem or proof. The added description of constant velocity as a first-order approximation is explanatory rather than a new derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, first contribution and conclusion explicitly broaden the framing from human reconstruction to human-object reconstruction and motion. The central claims concerning metric-scale reconstruction, feed-forward streaming, novel-view/novel-time synthesis and occlusion-aware fusion are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of template-method limitations, attributes LHM's latency to SMPL-X estimation, and motivates constant velocity as a small-interval approximation. Section 3.1 removes the explicit no-camera-motion condition without presenting a corresponding moving-camera evaluation. The existing limitations concerning large motions and long temporal intervals remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds an explanation of camera-head fine-tuning, and Appendix E documents timing hardware, inputs and latency/FPS definitions. The implementation summary no longer explicitly lists VGGT initialization of camera and point heads. V1's project/code link is replaced by a promise of future code and model release; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a dedicated discussion of template-based human reconstruction and animation, including LHM, LAM, GUAVA, AniGS, SMPL-X and FLAME. It substantially expands the positioning of Forge4D against parametric-template limitations in garment motion and human-object interaction. Additional references include Multi-HMR, MonoFusion and VVC.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. V2 condenses the abstract, standardizes 3DGS terminology, edits stage headings and updates author/affiliation information. The supplement gains a More Results section, receives the relocated ethics statement, and drops the LLM-usage statement; the acknowledgement is also removed.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different document template, with narrower text, revised typography, new title blocks and extensive resizing and relocation of displays. It adds the in-the-wild Figure 6/Table 3, ablation Figure 7 and timing Table 11. Existing appendix figures are retained with new numbering, while sensitivity tables are regrouped side by side.

improvement.justification: The in-the-wild evaluation and comparative timing strengthen evidence for practical applicability, while the added ablation images and quantitative flicker analysis better support temporal-coherence claims. These are incremental gains over v1's already substantial, retained experimental evidence. Less concrete code-access information and removal of the explicit fixed-camera qualification temper the improvement; changed fusion controls and timing hardware do not establish same-setting performance gains.
